_what: Member-site portrait candidates REJECTED by visual inspection for the WI legislature headshot import (migration 1482). Consumed by backend/scripts/discover-wi-legis-portraits.mjs — this file is the single source of truth, not a copy.
_why_this_exists: Portrait discovery on legis.wisconsin.gov member sites matches Umbraco media filenames against the member's name. That heuristic had a 29% defect rate: 23 of 79 filename hits were not headshots. A signature graphic and an official portrait are both '<surname>.png', so NO filename rule, aspect check, or file-size check distinguishes them. Only looking at the images does. Rejected members fall back to the official docs.legis roster portrait, which is 150x200 but is always a genuine tight headshot of the right person.
_method: All 79 filename-matched candidates were processed to the final 600x750 crop, tiled into contact sheets of 20, and inspected. Each rejection below was confirmed against the source filename.
_rule_of_thumb: An official low-resolution portrait beats a high-resolution wrong image. Do not trade correctness for sharpness.
_key_format: "<Chamber>-<district>" where Chamber is Assembly|Senate, matching essentials.office_current_holder keyed on (chamber, district) — never on name.
_reject_categories: signature graphic — a scanned/vector signature, often near-black or transparent
text wordmark / district header — branding with the member's name set as type
group or family photo — more than one person in frame
podium / press-conference shot — subject small, microphones, other people
event photo — commemorative or constituent-event imagery
website icon — a monogram or logo, not a photograph
